attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a router between lan-a (node2, 10.10.1.0/24 via eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.10.2.0/24 via eth2), with static addressing, per-subnet routes on node2/node3 pointing at node1, and a permissive forward filter — no NAT, so original source addresses are preserved. Verified bidirectional ping and TCP connectivity, and confirmed via tcpdump on node1's lan-b interface that node2's real 10.10.1.10 source address reaches node3 unmodified. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS reboot on node1, Alpine reboot on node2/node3), each proven via a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, with config persistence and cross-subnet connectivity re-verified after each recovery.
